concepts.title: Water Scarcity and the Need for Conservation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Water Scarcity and the Need for Conservation' refers to.
questions.a: Though three-fourths of the earth's surface is covered with water, only a small proportion is freshwater fit for use; rising populations, industry and irrigation multiply demand, and even high-rainfall regions like Cherapunji face shortages - making water conservation and management a national necessity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Water Scarcity and the Need for Conservation'.
questions.a: Plenty of water, little of it usable: scarcity is built by demand, waste and uneven supply.

concepts.title: Multipurpose River Projects and Water Disputes

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Multipurpose River Projects and Water Disputes' refers to.
questions.a: Independent India built dams as temples of modern progress - Bhakra-Nangal, Hirakud and Nagarjuna Sagar - serving irrigation, power, flood control and water supply; but large projects also displaced people, submerged forests and sparked river water disputes between states.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Multipurpose River Projects and Water Disputes'.
questions.a: Dams serve many purposes but carry many costs: benefits and displacements must be weighed together.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Multipurpose River Projects and Water Disputes' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: jess103.txt sections on multipurpose river projects and water disputes)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rainwater Harvesting and Traditional Systems' refers to.
questions.a: Long before pipes and dams, India harvested rain: khadins and johads in Rajasthan, rooftop tankas, bamboo drip irrigation in the northeast and inundation channels in flood plains; modern rooftop rainwater harvesting revives this wisdom, turning every roof into a catchment and every home into a water bank.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rainwater Harvesting and Traditional Systems'.
questions.a: Catch rain where it falls: rooftop harvesting and traditional structures store our own water.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rainwater Harvesting and Traditional Systems' taught, and from which source text?
